title: Promotions on the Audience Team
summary: We’re happy to share that Alexa Díaz and Jenna Fowler have been promoted to new roles. Please join us in congratulating them.
body_markdown:
Alexa Díaz has been promoted to editor, Social, and Jenna Fowler has been promoted to editor, Desk Audience and Coverage.


We’re happy to share that Alexa Díaz and Jenna Fowler have been promoted to new roles. Please join us in congratulating them.


Alexa Díaz has been promoted to editor, Social.


For the past two years, Alexa has been pivotal in shaping how our journalism is distributed from flagship accounts to a global audience of millions of users. This has included close collaboration with editors across the newsroom to deliver breaking news and showcase our signature journalism in an ever-changing social media landscape.


During that time, she also played a role in bringing our journalism to new platforms, including Snap, Bluesky and WhatsApp.


In her new role, Alexa will oversee a growing team of editors based around the world who shape how The Times appears across social platforms, particularly as we scale and deepen our video viewership off-platform. She’ll be a key partner to our video teams and audience editors who support video, and be the strategic partner to Social Visuals, Platform Partnerships and Product Marketing.


“No one has done more in recent years to make The Times an industry leader on social than Alexa,” said Jake Grovum, deputy audience director for coverage. “Her unique mix of excellent news judgment, social expertise and boundless creativity — plus an unmatched ability to bring out the best in her team — is exactly what The Times needs to keep setting the standard for journalistic excellence on social for years to come.”


Alexa came to The Times in 2020 from The Los Angeles Times, where she worked as an audience engagement editor and reporter. She got her start on the NYT Kids team before joining the newsroom social team in 2022. The most delightful project she has worked on for The Times so far was a board game about bees for 9-year-olds that was rooted in science reporting.


— Anna Dubenko and Meg Ely


Credit: Earl Wilson


Jenna Fowler, a razor-sharp audience editor who has led the team’s elections planning for the past three cycles, has been promoted to editor, Desk Audience and Coverage.


In this new role, Jenna will be a leader across a team of desk editors embedded across nearly every department in the newsroom. She’ll partner with me to ensure audience editors working across the report continue to arm their desks with smart analysis, actionable insights and up-to-date best practices.


Jenna has set the bar for an embedded audience editor, and proven to be an empathetic manager and mentor to colleagues on the team. After joining The Times as an S.E.O. editor in 2021, Jenna quickly established herself as a go-to authority on all things audience, with the news judgment, creativity and collaborative nature to turn insights into action, making our report sharper and growing our audience in the process.


“Jenna’s an outstanding newsroom advocate for the Audience team and its insights into our readers,” said Mohammed Hadi, news director. “It’s hard not to catch her enthusiasm for the subject. She translates data into journalism, meaning it’s easy to walk away from a conversation with her full of new ideas.”


In recent years, Jenna has embedded with both the Politics desk and the Washington bureau, working on some of the most high-profile and high-pressure stories we’ve covered, in addition to leading the Audience team’s 2024 election planning and this year’s midterms. Last year, she was promoted to senior audience editor, overseeing the work of desk audience editors on key news desks.


Now, Jenna will partner with me as we shape our growing team, in addition to managing desk audience editors for the Magazine, Graphics/Weather/The Upshot and Special Projects, and guiding the entire team’s work supporting the journalism we produce every day.


— Jake Grovum


Credit: Earl Wilson
